answer: A registry that requires each agent to stake a costly, time-locked bond works like a saffron merchant's seal: the bond is a relic of past honest work, not a fresh claim. New identities must hold their stake through a slow pulse of verified transactions before they can earn, so a Sybil attacker pays a real deposit and weeks of waiting per fake identity, while honest agents keep trading. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a thousand becomes ruinous.
